classification.difficultyReason: Unscaffolded fencing model. The student counts the 4 and 2 fence segments from the diagram, eliminates a variable, and maximises a quadratic. This is essentially the same demand as the three-sided netting question.

content.prompt: A farmer has 480 m of fencing to build a rectangular enclosure divided into three pens by two internal fences, as shown. What are the dimensions of the enclosure that give the greatest total area?

answer.short: The internal fences are 60 m long and the enclosure is 120 m wide: 60 m by 120 m (greatest area $7200\text{ m}^2$).
answer.worked:
Let $x$ m be the length of each of the four fences running the same way as the internal fences, and $y$ m the length of each of the other two.
$$\begin{aligned}4x+2y&=480\\y&=240-2x\\A(x)&=x(240-2x)\\A(x)&=240x-2x^2,\qquad 0<x<120\\A'(x)&=240-4x.\end{aligned}$$
Setting $A'(x)=0$ gives $x=60$.
$$\begin{aligned}A''(x)&=-4<0\\y&=240-2(60)=120\\A(60)&=60(120)=7200.\end{aligned}$$
The quadratic opens downwards, so this is the global maximum. The enclosure should be 60 m by 120 m, giving a total area of $7200\text{ m}^2$.
